name: Field-level encryption
needs: encrypt sensitive fields in my database
if someone steals a backup they shouldn't read user notes
store tokens for third-party services safely
summary: Encrypting chosen columns in your app before they reach the database, with a key the database never sees. A stolen backup or database dump then shows ciphertext for those fields. It needs a plan for keys, rotation and search.
need_when: You store very sensitive text (health, legal, financial notes), government ids, or access tokens for other services.
skip_when: Your host's disk encryption covers your threat and the data isn't especially sensitive. Fields you must search or sort on are hard to encrypt.

ways.title: An encrypted field type in your framework
ways.how: Rails Active Record Encryption, Laravel encrypted casts, or a Django field built on Fernet from the cryptography package.
ways.tradeoff: Transparent in code. Encrypted fields can't be filtered or sorted in SQL.

ways.title: Envelope encryption with a KMS
ways.how: AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Vault wrap per-record data keys. Your app encrypts with the data key.
ways.tradeoff: Strong key control and audit. More moving parts and latency.

ways.title: Database-side encryption functions
ways.tradeoff: Easy to add. The key travels to the database in queries and may show up in logs.

prompt:
Add field-level encryption for sensitive columns.

Requirements:
- Columns: [list]. Encrypt in the app with [Fernet / AES-GCM] before saving and decrypt on read.
- The key comes from an environment secret separate from other app secrets, never from the database.
- Prefix each stored value with a version tag so I can tell encrypted from plain and rotate keys later.
- Rotation: a new key encrypts, old keys still decrypt, and a background command re-encrypts rows in batches.
- If a value can't be decrypted, show a placeholder and keep the stored ciphertext untouched on save.
- Encrypt existing rows with a migration that runs in batches and can resume.
- For fields I need to look up exactly, store a separate keyed hash (HMAC) for lookups.
- Keep decrypted values out of logs, error reports and analytics.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Reading the table directly shows ciphertext for each listed column.
2. After rotating, old rows still read and the re-encrypt command upgrades them.
3. Starting the app with the wrong key shows placeholders, not crashes, and saving doesn't destroy data.
4. Error reports contain no decrypted values.
5. A restore from backup is readable only with the key.
acceptance_checks: Reading the table directly shows ciphertext for each listed column.
After rotating, old rows still read and the re-encrypt command upgrades them.
Starting the app with the wrong key shows placeholders, not crashes, and saving doesn't destroy data.
Error reports contain no decrypted values.
A restore from backup is readable only with the key.
if_you_skip_it: A leaked backup or read-only database breach exposes the most private data you hold.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal encrypts sensitive text and JSON columns with Fernet before they reach Postgres, using its own field encryption key setting rather than the main app secret. Stored values carry a version prefix, older keys stay decrypt-only for rotation, and a value that can't be decrypted shows a placeholder while the original ciphertext is kept on save.
